name: Saudavi
tagline: Deep thinker, quiet strength, and loyal to the very end.
share_line: I notice everything, plan everything, and remember what you said last year.

free.summary:
In Unani tradition, Earth (Saudavi) is the mizaj of sauda, black bile, the cool and dry humour linked with earth and autumn. If you are Earth, you are the person who reads the fine print, notices the cracked tile nobody else saw, and quietly keeps track of everyone's appointments, passport expiry dates and passwords. You think before you speak, and when you do speak, it usually matters.

You are serious, careful and deeply loyal. You take promises to heart, and you would rather do one thing well than ten things badly. The flip side is that worry can creep in, small things can turn into big overthinking sessions, and you sometimes keep your feelings so private that loved ones can't tell what's wrong.

Physically, Unani texts picture the Earth person as lean, with dry skin, lighter sleep and a sensitivity to cold. Many Earth people find they feel calmer and more grounded with warm, moist, nourishing food, a regular routine, oil massage and enough rest, especially as autumn turns to winter.
traits: Thoughtful and analytical; you weigh every option before you decide.
Detail-oriented and reliable; people trust you with the things that really matter.
Deeply loyal; once you are someone's friend, you're friends for life.
Private with feelings; you show love through actions far more than words.
Prone to worry and overthinking, especially late at night.
High standards for yourself, sometimes to the point of being your own harshest critic.
body_signs: Unani texts describe a lean, lighter frame that can find it hard to gain weight.
Skin, hair and lips tend towards dryness, especially in winter and in centrally heated rooms.
Hands and feet often feel cold, and chilly, windy weather is your least favourite.
Sleep is often light, and a busy mind can keep it waiting.
Digestion can feel unsettled when meals are skipped, irregular or too dry.
Joints and muscles may feel stiff on cold mornings until you get moving.
free.quick_tip: Never skip breakfast, and make it warm and moist: porridge with milk, an egg, or toast with a little butter or olive oil. Unani tradition suggests regular, warm, nourishing meals are the simplest way to soften a cool, dry temperament.

premium.deep_dive:
In the Canon, Ibn Sina described sauda as the heaviest of the humours: cool, dry and settling, the sediment that gives the body structure and the mind depth. An Earth (Saudavi) person, in this picture, carries a little more of that grounded, mountain-like quality. It is the temperament of focus, endurance and seriousness, and it asks for warmth and moisture to stay light.

In the body, Unani tradition associates this mizaj with a lean build, dry skin, cold hands and feet, light sleep and a digestion that dislikes irregular meals. Cold and dryness are your weak points: skipped meals, too much tea or coffee, cold dry winds, stale or very sour food, and long nights of worry are all traditionally believed to add to sauda. When the balance tips, many Earth people notice dry skin, stiffness, poor sleep and a heaviness of mood. The traditional answer is warmth, moisture and regularity: freshly cooked food, healthy fats like olive oil, butter or ghee and almonds in moderation, oil massage (dalk), warm baths and a steady daily rhythm.

In the mind, coolness gives calm and dryness gives precision. You notice details, think in systems and remember what others forget. You are often the person who reads the tenancy agreement twice, checks the wedding caterer's contract or plans the budget for the holidays. The risk is rumination: replaying a comment for days, or waiting for a certainty that never comes.

Emotionally, the tradition describes Earth people as sensitive, loyal and inward. The very word melancholy comes from the Greek for black bile, but that is only half the story; since ancient times this temperament has also been linked with scholars, poets and careful craftspeople. Your feelings run deep and slow. The task is to let them out regularly, so they don't harden into silence.

Across life stages, Unani tradition saw middle age onwards as naturally cooler and drier, so a young Earth person may seem older than their years, the serious one at the family gathering. The warm, moist years of youth are often when you feel most balanced. From your forties, staying warm, nourished and active becomes especially important.

Across the seasons, autumn is your mirror. Tradition linked sauda with the cool, dry months when leaves fall, and many Earth people feel a dip in mood and energy as the days shorten, especially far from the equator. A long winter can feel harsh, spring is often restoring, and summer's warmth can actually suit you as long as you stay hydrated. Living well as an Earth person means adding warmth and softness to a strong, steady core.

foods_limit.item: Leftovers and batch-cooked food day after day
foods_limit.why: Tradition favours fresh cooking; stale food is believed to add heaviness and dryness.

foods_limit.item: Strong tea and coffee, cup after cup
foods_limit.why: Drying in effect; too many cups can leave you wired, parched and sleepless.

foods_limit.item: Very sour foods: pickles, tamarind, unripe mango
foods_limit.why: Sharp, sour flavours are traditionally believed to increase dryness and sauda.

foods_limit.item: Dry snacks: rusks, crackers, crisps and pretzels
foods_limit.why: Dry on dry; they leave an Earth system thirsty and unsatisfied.
Cold on cold; they work against the warmth you need, especially in winter.

foods_limit.item: Cured meats, salted fish and aged, salty cheese
foods_limit.why: Classical texts link preserved, salted foods with an increase in sauda.

drinks: Warm milk with saffron or cardamom at bedtime: warm, moist and settling
Turmeric milk (golden milk) on cold evenings: warming, nourishing and a cosy ritual
Chicken soup in a mug: warming and moistening on cold evenings
Green tea with cardamom and a little honey: warm and light, gentler than strong tea or coffee
Warm water through the day: you forget to drink, and dryness follows
Fresh grape or sweet pomegranate juice at room temperature: moistening and refreshing
spices_herbs: Saffron: traditionally counted as mufarreh, believed to lift the spirits; a few strands in milk or rice
Green cardamom: fragrant and warming, lovely in milk, coffee, tea and baking
Cinnamon: warms cool hands and slow mornings, in tea or porridge
Fresh ginger: traditionally warm and gently moist, kinder to you than dried, sharp spices
Fennel: many people find it settles digestion after meals
Go easy on red chilli and sharp, sour seasonings like sumac or dried mango powder: they add to your natural dryness

daily_routine.morning: Wake at a regular time every day, neither too early after a late night nor too late. Start with warm water, then a warm, moist breakfast: porridge with milk, a soft-boiled egg or toast with a little butter. Before your shower, try a quick oil massage on hands, feet and scalp with almond or olive oil, a classic Unani practice (dalk) for dryness.
daily_routine.midday: Eat lunch on time; irregular meals are traditionally believed to unsettle an Earth system. Choose warm, freshly cooked food: soup, vegetables with a little olive oil, a warm grain bowl. Step outside for some daylight, even on a grey day. Cap yourself at two cups of tea or coffee by mid-afternoon.
daily_routine.evening: Evenings are when worry tends to creep in, so plan something warm and social: a walk with a friend, time with family or a hobby that uses your hands. Eat a warm, early dinner. Write tomorrow's worries in a notebook so your mind doesn't carry them to bed.
daily_routine.sleep: Sleep is precious for you and often light. Keep a fixed bedtime, put the phone away 45 minutes before, and try warm milk with saffron or cardamom. A warm foot soak, or a little oil rubbed into the soles, is a traditional winding-down habit. Aim for seven to eight unbroken hours.

seasons.summer: Summer warmth can actually suit you, but heat plus your natural dryness makes dehydration a risk, especially in a dry, desert-style summer. Drink water steadily, enjoy sweet mangoes, grapes and yogurt drinks in moderation, and avoid long hours in direct sun. Keep meals regular even when your appetite dips, and don't survive on iced coffee and crisps.
seasons.rains: Humid, rainy weather often feels softening to a dry mizaj. Enjoy it, but eat freshly cooked food. Grey days can bring a dip in mood, especially if you live somewhere they stretch on for weeks, so plan cosy, social things: tea with an old friend, a family film night, or cooking something warm together.
seasons.winter: Your hardest season, especially if you live somewhere with long, dark winters. Cold winds, dry indoor heating and short days are traditionally believed to increase sauda, so many Earth people feel stiffer, drier and lower now. Lean on warm, moist food: soups, eggs, olive oil or butter, carrots and soaked dried fruit. Oil your skin, keep your feet warm, and seek daylight and company as deliberately as a winter coat.
seasons.spring: Spring is often your recovery season, as warmth and moisture return. Many Earth people feel lighter in mood and more sociable. Use the energy: start a new habit, reconnect with friends and enjoy the weddings, parties and festivals, even if you sit out a dance or two.

premium.movement: Your body likes steady, gentle, regular movement more than intense bursts. Walking, light jogging, stretching, swimming in a warm pool and cycling all suit you. Unani tradition cautions a cool, dry mizaj against exhausting exercise that dries you out further, so stop at pleasant tiredness, not collapse. Warm up properly on cold mornings and stretch afterwards. Exercising outdoors in morning daylight, or with a friend, does double duty: it warms your body and lifts your mood at the same time.
premium.emotional_balance: Unani counts the emotions among the six essential factors of health, and tradition specifically links worry, grief and long brooding with increased sauda. For you, emotional care is not a luxury. Build daily habits of release: write things down, talk to one trusted person, spend time with people who make you laugh. Limit late-night scrolling and news, which feeds rumination. Practise noticing good things, even three small ones before sleep. Prayer, meditation or time in nature, whatever fits your beliefs, brings calm to many people. If low mood, worry or sleeplessness lasts more than two weeks, please speak to a doctor or qualified counsellor. Asking for help is wise, not weak.
premium.fasting: Long fasts can leave an Earth body extra dry, so prepare well, whether you fast for faith or tradition, keep a weekly fast day or follow an intermittent-fasting window. Before the fast, choose warm, moist food: porridge with milk, eggs, bread with a little butter or olive oil, a few soaked dates or figs, and water sipped steadily. Skip very salty or dry food. Break the fast with water or warm milk, then eat a nourishing meal rather than a plate of fried snacks, and get to bed as early as you can.

when_out_of_balance: Lying awake replaying conversations or worrying about things that haven't happened.
Skin, lips and heels getting unusually dry and rough.
Pulling away from family and friends, and feeling heavier in mood.
Feeling stiff and cold even when others are comfortable.
Becoming extra critical of yourself or others over small mistakes.

with_other_mizaj.damvi: Unani tradition sees this as a near-perfect balance of opposites: the warmth and moisture of Air (Damvi) meet your coolness and dryness. Air lifts your mood and draws you into family life; you give them depth and stability. Don't dismiss their cheerfulness as shallowness, and let them help you laugh at your worries.
with_other_mizaj.safravi: With Fire (Safravi) you share dryness: both of you value logic, standards and getting things right. Their warmth can energise your plans, and your caution can save them from hasty decisions. Watch for criticism on both sides. Make a habit of appreciation, and keep tough discussions short, specific and kind.
with_other_mizaj.balghami: With Water (Balghami), a quiet, loyal, steady pairing. Their soft, moist calm eases your dryness and worry, and your careful planning gives their easygoing nature direction. The risk is a home that is too still. Plan warm, social things together, such as dinners with friends, family visits and shared hobbies, so neither of you retreats too far.
with_other_mizaj.saudavi: Two Earth people, whether spouses, siblings or colleagues, understand each other's silences, standards and need for order, and you can build deep, lasting trust. The risk is double the worry and too little lightness. Take turns being the optimist, invite cheerful friends and family over often, and talk about feelings before they harden into distance.
